files_reviewed: README.md (grep for env, mock and security claims)
note: No .env or .env.example is committed (.env* is gitignored). The OpenAI call runs only on the server, so there is no ai_browser_call. prompts.js is empty. The system prompt lives in agent.js. All customers, orders and refunds are in-memory mock data. The README says refunds are simulated, but the UI and API return 'Refund processed successfully' with no caveat. | Second labeler: No database, so database_rules does not apply. The model is called only server-side and no NEXT_PUBLIC env var exists, so no ai_browser_call. No .env file is committed because .gitignore covers .env*. CSS files, public SVGs, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING and GITHUB_SETUP were not reviewed. README demo scenario uses CUS-1002 while the admin page uses CUS-1015.

labels.what: 15 hardcoded orders serve as the CRM. All delivery dates are in Jul-Aug 2026, so the 7-day window check against the real clock now denies the demo 'successful refund' order ORD-2001
15 fake customers with example.com emails and placeholder +91-90000000xx phones, used as the customer database
Hardcoded demo scenarios with an expectedDecision field. The page later shows expectedDecision as the real result (see fake_action labels)
getCustomer tool reads the hardcoded customers array, not a CRM
getOrder tool reads the hardcoded orders array
getCustomerOrders tool filters the hardcoded orders array
processRefund sets refundStatus on the in-memory order and returns a made-up REF-<timestamp> id with 'Refund processed successfully'. No payment provider is called and the change is lost on restart

On an OpenAI 429 or quota error the agent silently switches to a regex script that pulls CUS-/ORD- ids from the last message and runs the refund chain. The home page (src/app/page.js 63-68) sells this as a reliable agent
Prompt says always run checkRefundEligibility before approving. processRefund never checks that eligibility ran or passed, so the model can call it directly
Prompt says never override the refund policy. processRefund does not check the 7-day window, non-refundable categories, damaged-item verification or order ownership
Tool description says process a refund only after eligibility is confirmed and the amount calculated. The execute code enforces neither
Prompt says do not claim a refund was processed unless the tool confirms it. The final model text goes to the customer with no check against tool results
processRefund runs as soon as the model calls it. There is no staff approval and no customer confirm step before money would move
Damaged items return eligible true with requiresVerification true. Nothing reads requiresVerification, so the fallback agent refunds any damaged item inside the 7-day window with no verification step
processRefund checks only amount > 0, amount <= order amount and not already refunded. It takes no customerId, so there is no ownership check, no eligibility check and no per-session refund cap

Two checkRefundEligibility functions disagree. refund-policy.js denies damaged items and checks not-yet-delivered, while policy-validator.js (the one the tools import) approves damaged items and floors the day count
refundWindowDays = 7 in code, repeated as literal text in lines 9 and 88, so a policy change needs three edits
Currency INR hardcoded in calculateRefund and again in processRefund (line 83)
maxIterations 6 and model gpt-4o-mini hardcoded

When the API returns no decision, the admin card shows the scenario's expectedDecision. The OpenAI path never returns a decision, so the dashboard shows APPROVED or DENIED from the script, not from the agent
On an API error the catch block sets the decision to expectedDecision, so a failed run still shows the expected outcome
Refund Mode shows 'Live' because refund.mode is never set, even though every refund is mock
'System online' badge is static text with no health check
'Online' status is static text with no health check
Admin dashboard has no login or role check, and its Run button triggers real refund processing through /api/agent
/api/agent has no authentication. Anyone can request refunds
The only identity is a customer id typed in chat (sequential CUS-1001 style). getCustomer returns that customer's email and phone, and refunds run for whoever names the id
The client sends the whole messages array and the server passes it into the model conversation as-is. A caller can inject system, assistant or tool messages to override the rules
No rate limit and no size limit on the messages array for a paid OpenAI endpoint (up to 6 model calls per request)
Raw error.message is returned to the client
Falls back to OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY for ordinary chat calls, so an admin-scoped key could serve public traffic
calculateRefund returns the full hardcoded order amount in INR. No real order or payment system, no partial refunds or fees
checkRefundEligibility runs real rule logic but only over the hardcoded customers and orders arrays
On a 429 or quota error runAgent silently swaps the model for runLocalAgent, a regex script that pulls CUS- and ORD- ids and runs the refund flow. The chat UI does not show which mode answered
processRefund runs straight from a model tool call. No customer confirmation and no staff approval before the refund
Damaged products return eligible true with requiresVerification true. Nothing in the app reads requiresVerification, so the agent and the fallback refund damaged items with no verification step
Customer identity is whatever CUS- id the user types. Nothing proves the requester owns the account, and ids are sequential, so any customer's order can be refunded
Non-refundable categories are hardcoded. README lists only Digital and Personalized
Client-supplied messages array is spread into the conversation with no role check. A caller can inject a system message or forge assistant and tool turns, such as a fake eligibility result
